extracted.intended_audience: agency staff, regulated entities, stakeholders, legal practitioners, and members of the public seeking a concise summary of the Administrative Procedure Act
extracted.subtask_description: A concise summary of the Administrative Procedure Act requirements that govern how federal agencies develop and issue regulations, including publication, public comment, timing of effectiveness, coverage of other agency actions, and standards for judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notices in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA includes requirements for publishing notices of proposed and final rulemaking in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide public notice of proposed and final rules by publishing appropriate notices in the Federal Register so that the regulated public and other stakeholders are informed of regulatory actions. This is the procedural mechanism that triggers other APA requirements such as public comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public comment (notice-and-comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA provides opportunities for the public to comment on notices of proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory proposals are subject to a notice-and-comment process: publishing a proposal and allowing the public to submit comments. This process ensures transparency and input from affected parties before a rule is finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed effective date for most rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA requires most rules to have a 30-day delayed effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a general rule, agencies must allow a 30-day period between publication of a final rule and its effective date to give regulated parties time to comply. (The summary states the general requirement; agencies may rely on statutory exceptions or other legal doctrines in particular circumstances.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope beyond rulemaking (other agency actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to setting forth rulemaking procedures, the APA addresses other agency actions such as issuance of policy statements, licenses, and permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The APA's procedures and standards can apply to a variety of agency actions, not only formal rulemaking. Practitioners should consider whether a given agency act (policy statements, licensing decisions, permitting) falls within APA procedural or review provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA provides standards for judicial review if a person has been adversely affected or aggrieved by an agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals or entities adversely affected by agency actions can seek review under the APA. The statute supplies the legal standards and procedures courts use to assess agency decisions (e.g., reviewability, standards of deference, remedies), which determine when and how agency actions can be challenged.
